chapter: Coleman Hawkins, Bernie Young and doubling on tenor
title: Bernie Young at the Wisconsin Roof Garden
summary: He played about six months in Wisconsin and later at the Wisconsin Roof Garden, a hotel job that lasted several years; he was in Newark with Rex Stewart when they sent for him.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, when you -- when you -- now, just when -- when you went with Bernie Young back, didn't you go to
How long did you play there?
I played there for about six months. I came back to the Wisconsin Roof Garden. When I came back --
Yeah. Roof garden on a hotel?
That must have been a fairly good job for those days.

Yes, it was. We stayed there for about, oh, I think about four or five years. They sent for me when I was in New Jersey working in Newark, and they sent for me (unintelligible) but I'm doing good and liked the East too (unintelligible) and living in New York and working over in Newark. Rex Stewart and myself, we were good buddies, Walter Johnson (unintelligible) going.
